evidence.description: The selected result labels its scope as the 18 retained visits and uses the matching subset denominator; the stated rate 7/18 = 0.3889 is arithmetically correct and consistent with the accounting (24 planned, 18 retained, 6 removed, 7 events), which I independently verified against inputs/data.csv (18 rows with water_depth_cm >= 10; 7 of those with egg_mass_detected = yes).

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Among the 18 retained vernal pool survey visits (the scientific target), wood frog egg masses were detected on 7 visits, a detection rate of 7/18 = 0.3889 per retained visit.

- Planned survey visits: 24
- Retained after screening (water depth >= 10 cm): 18
- Removed by screening (water depth < 10 cm): 6
- Egg mass detection events among retained visits: 7

evidence.description: The report closes by restating the scope restriction, explicitly forbidding a complete-domain reading of the subset rate.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict by searching the report for any sentence that attributes the 0.3889 rate to the complete planned set of 24 visits, and by checking whether the denominator (18) could silently be presented as if it were the planned count. Every scope statement (study design line 7, selected result line 18, closing line 20) restricts the claim to the retained subset, and the accounting section separately and correctly reports the planned count of 24 and the 6 removed visits. I also recomputed all counts from inputs/data.csv and found no discrepancy that could mask a scope substitution. The falsification attempt failed; the issue class is not present.
